description: Bidirectional BFS finds a path with the fewest edges. It runs breadth-first search forwards from the start and backwards from the goals, one whole layer at a time, and stops when a new layer meets the other side. `bidirectional_bfs` always grows the smaller frontier and returns the shortest meet of that layer. Edge costs do not guide the search; the reported cost is the sum of the costs along the returned path. On graphs where each state has many successors, it expands far fewer states than one-sided breadth-first search, but it needs the predecessors of each state.
